A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ERC-loss work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original 3B- and 15B-parameter pre-training experiments, downstream evaluations, throughput measurements, and ablation and parameter analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results in Section 4 and the reorganized appendices.

M1.justification: The proxy-token construction, bounded multiplicative noise, activation-norm matrix, two ERC constraints, and inference procedure are unchanged. The pseudocode correction aligns its implementation with the existing loss rather than introducing a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Dolma training sample, ten evaluation tasks for the 3B models, and eight benchmarks for the 15B models. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Vanilla MoE and Autonomy-of-Experts remain the 3B comparators; the 15B comparison still excludes AoE because of its cost. The router-orthogonalization comparator is retained when its experiment moves into Section 4.5.

E3.justification: Reported training budgets, architectures, optimizer settings, evaluation measures, and ablation configurations are unchanged. This includes 500B training tokens for the 3B models and the existing alpha sweeps; relocated experiments introduce no new protocols.

E4.justification: All five analyses are retained: activation choice, noise removal, router orthogonalization, alpha greater than one, and parameter norms. V1 Appendices C.1–C.3 move to Section 4.5, while C.4–C.5 become v2 Appendices A.1–A.2. Their empirical evidence is unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for benchmark performance. Table 3 retains the same parameter-norm means and standard deviations, which describe variation across parameters rather than repeated-training uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the matched performance, specialization, and ablation plots retain their results. For example, Table 1 reports MMLU scores of 63.2 for MoE and 64.6 with ERC in both versions. Throughput measurements and qualitative findings also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V1 Appendix C.5 becomes v2 Appendix A.2 with a revised norm-scaling argument: an explicit weighted columnwise cosine definition replaces the informal vector–matrix angle, the worked example scales router norms, and a fixed column-to-matrix norm-ratio assumption is added. The noise-bound and FLOPs derivations remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: efficient expert–router coupling, improved downstream performance, and controllable, measurable expert specialization. Neither the claimed experimental scope nor the novelty claim changes.

C2.justification: The revised norm-manipulation explanation explicitly conditions its expert-norm argument on fixed relative column norms. This qualifies the previously broader explanation. Interpretations concerning specialization trade-offs, noise generalization, and limited benefits from router orthogonalization are otherwise retained.

D1.justification: The pseudocode, Figure 7 in v1 and Figure 8 in v2, replaces the undefined A with M when constructing the diagonal mask and adds the experts.Wg tensor shape, (n, D, d). These improve implementation guidance without changing reported experimental settings.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds a short discussion of mixtures of attention heads or entire layers, citing Gong et al.'s Mixture-of-Modules and Lin et al.'s Mixture of In-Context Experts. Existing references and the central positioning against prior coupling methods are retained.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative and appendix organization are substantially rearranged: Section 4.5 replaces its brief overview with three full ablation discussions, and the remaining analyses become a leading FAQ appendix before the noise derivation and efficiency analysis. Additional prose edits are mostly grammatical.

P2.justification: The four-panel appendix Figure 6 is repackaged into a three-panel main-text figure and a separate Figure 7 beside Table 2. Figure 5 and Tables 1 and 3 are relocated, with captions and cross-references adjusted. The underlying plots and overall visual style are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 makes existing ablation evidence easier to follow and improves implementation guidance by correcting the undefined pseudocode variable and documenting the tensor shape. These are limited gains with unchanged empirical support. The revised norm argument is not a complete theoretical repair: its signed cosine sum does not generally reproduce the L2 activation norm, leaving the general guarantee insufficiently justified.
